summary: Verification round for the 8 targeted GridLock fixes + light regression. Backend: existing pytest suite 10/10 PASS (GET /api/, POST+GET /api/demo-requests, POST+GET /api/sim-runs, validation, CORS, no _id). FIX 1 PASS (30 trials, two Run Comparison clicks gave seed 325456 -> +40.8% (baseline 792.6t / system 469.1t) and seed 568040 -> +1.3% (651.6t / 642.9t); values differ, seed shown in caption, GET /api/sim-runs went 12 -> 14 with matching rows). FIX 2 PASS (baseline_avg > system_avg, improvement positive both runs). FIX 3 PASS (Choke-Point: collision 7->8 and deadlock 1->3 over 71 ticks, i.e. counters flat while the same standoff persisted - no per-tick inflation). FIX 4/5/6 PARTIAL (CRITICAL correctly releases task, logs 'Rx CRITICAL - routing to charging point [x,17]', reallocation indicator climbed 0->10, and battery only rises at the charging cell with 'fully charged, back to service' - but under a long Free Operation run at 20 t/s ALL FOUR robots ended DEAD at 0% by ~tick 810 and never recovered; see rca). FIX 7 PASS (target-R1..R4 markers on landing hero and dashboard grid, planned-path dots still render). FIX 8 PASS (landing nav + footer + dashboard header all read GridLock, no AMR-FLEET, title 'GridLock · Decentralized AMR Fleet Coordination'). Regression PASS: play/pause, step (+1), reset (->0), all 9 scenario cards, add/kill/recover/remove, MIN_FLEET_SIZE toast ('Minimum fleet size is 3 - cannot remove R3'), inject-1/4/8, block-choke, regen-fixed/random, roster search/status-filter/robot-detail, event-log search + CSV (event_log.csv), demo-mode-toggle hides admin+roster. Iteration_1's HIGH battery-panel/performance-panel overflow is FIXED, and blocked_noalt now produces reallocation=2.

minor.issue: email still a plain str (no format validation) and creates return 200 not 201 - accepted as intentional per this round's scope.

ui_bugs.issue: HIGH: Fleet-wide battery death. Free Operation at 20 t/s: by tick ~810 all 4 robots were battery 0% / status 'error' (roster R1 9,15 / R2 13,15 / R3 7,15 / R4 13,16 - all one or two cells short of the charging row y=17) and the sim never recovers (Battery Overview 0 NORMAL / 4 DEAD, deadlock indicator 60). Event log shows R2, R3 and R4 all being routed to the SAME charging cell [7,17]: _nearestCharging() picks the nearest cell with no occupancy/reservation check, so multiple CRITICAL robots converge on one cell, deadlock in the charging approach, keep draining WAIT_BATTERY_COST while stalled, hit 0% and die - and each dead robot then becomes a static obstacle on the charging approach, cascading to the rest of the fleet. Also the CRITICAL threshold (10% = ~18 moves at MOVE_BATTERY_COST 0.55) leaves almost no margin to cross the warehouse. Charging itself works when a robot arrives alone ('R3 fully charged, back to service').
LOW/testability: individual log lines have no data-testid (only log-search / export-log-btn / clear-log-filter), so a test cannot assert per-row content; filtering had to be verified visually.

issues: Measured improvement variance across fresh seeds is very wide (observed +40.8% then +1.3% at 30 trials). Honest, but for a jury demo a single unlucky seed shows 'below 20% target' - consider showing a mean +/- spread over a couple of seed batches, or displaying both the last run and a rolling average.

action_items: HIGH: Prevent fleet-wide battery death - make charging-point selection reserve/skip occupied or already-targeted cells (per-robot assignment of distinct warehouse.zones.charging cells), and/or raise the CRITICAL threshold (or lower WAIT_BATTERY_COST) so a robot can always reach its assigned charger. Also consider not letting a dead robot become an obstacle inside the charging row.
MEDIUM: Verify recovery path - once all robots are dead nothing in the UI restores service except Reset; consider auto-tow/auto-recover or a clear 'fleet down' state.
LOW: Add data-testid to event-log rows for assertable log filtering.
NOTE: No action needed on FIX 1/2/3/7/8 - all verified working; iteration_1's panel-overflow and blocked_noalt reallocation issues are resolved.
critical_code_review_comments: engine.js:684 _nearestCharging() is stateless - it ignores whether another robot already targets or occupies that cell, which is the direct cause of the observed multi-robot pile-up at [7,17]. Track assigned charging cells (Set) and pick the nearest free one.

engine.js:671 CRITICAL branch fires only when battery_state === CRITICAL (<10%); with MOVE_BATTERY_COST 0.55 that is ~18 moves of range, less than the warehouse diagonal (24x18). The reserve should be distance-aware (route when battery < cost_to_nearest_charger * safety_factor).

engine.js:871 robots keep draining WAIT_BATTERY_COST while blocked en route to a charger, so a charging-row standoff is guaranteed to end in death; consider zero/reduced drain when status===CHARGING and stalled.
engine.js is now 1261 lines - still well over the 700-line guideline; split pathfinding / collision+deadlock / battery+charging / task-allocation.
PerformancePanel.run() still swallows the /api/sim-runs POST error (empty catch) - a backend outage is invisible to the operator.
seed_data_creation: 2 real sim-run rows persisted by the UI (seeds 325456 and 568040) plus the TEST_ demo-request/sim-run rows created by the pytest suite.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run backend suite: cd /app && python -m pytest backend/tests/backend_test.py -v --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_results.xml (10/10 currently). RETEST FOCUS after fix: run Free Operation at 20 t/s for ~60s and assert the fleet never reaches 4 DEAD, that distinct CRITICAL robots are routed to DISTINCT charging cells, and that each reaches its charger (battery rises only at the charging cell).
rca_of_the_issue: Fleet-wide battery death: engine._handleBattery() (line 671) routes a CRITICAL robot to engine._nearestCharging() (line 684), which is a pure Manhattan-nearest lookup over warehouse.zones.charging with no occupancy or reservation state. When several robots go CRITICAL around the same time they all receive the same target (observed: R2, R3, R4 all -> [7,17]). They converge on the single approach cell, the collision/deadlock resolver makes losers wait, and waiting robots still drain CONFIG.WAIT_BATTERY_COST (engine.js:871), so the losers hit 0%, go DEAD, and the DEAD branch (line 667) writes their cell into this.dynamic as a permanent obstacle - directly on the charging approach - which blocks the next CRITICAL robot. The cascade ended with all 4 robots DEAD at 0% one or two cells short of the y=17 charging row (tick ~810, deadlock indicator 60). Reproduce: /dashboard, Free Operation, click speed-slider and press ArrowRight to 20 t/s, Play, poll [data-testid=battery-panel] every 4s for ~50s. Mitigation: assign distinct charging cells (reservation set), make the CRITICAL trigger distance-aware, and/or suppress drain for stalled robots already committed to charging.
